_what_this_file_is: The REQUIREMENTS half of V5 section 14's identity split. It answers 'what must a
deployment be for this qualification to apply to it' -- and nothing about any
particular build.
IT CONTAINS NO DIGEST OF ANY FILE IN THIS REPOSITORY. That is the property the
split exists for, and it is checked mechanically by
qualification/runners/build-manifest.py --check-expected. Before this file, the
identity was a hash over `deployment.inputs`, and five of those inputs were
digests of files in the SAME tree that recorded them. So editing a profile, a
preset, a spec or a graph dump moved the identity, adopting the move was another
edit, and the identity has moved four times in one wave. A correct change moving
the identity is the definition of the defect: S1's `includeShippedRoot: false`
is authorized by the round-2 brief, and it moved `host_profile_digest` anyway.
WHAT REPLACES THE BUILD-DERIVED HALF. A generated BuildManifest, stored as a
qualification/release artifact rather than a source input of the candidate it
describes:
RuntimeDeploymentIdentity     = H(canonical BuildManifest)
QualificationContractIdentity = H(RuntimeDeploymentIdentity
+ acceptance_definition_digest
+ release_runner_digests)
and result/evidence files bind to QualificationContractIdentity. See
qualification/results/P14-manifest/STEP1-SOURCE-MAP.md for the input-by-input
map of what moved where.
WHY THIS FILE IS NOT JUST 'THE LOCK, MINUS THE DIGESTS'. `deployment.inputs` also
carried fields that are neither a requirement nor a build fact -- a redacted
argument string, a trust-model name, an authority-policy sentence. Those are
carried here where they are genuinely a REQUIREMENT on any deployment, and are
recorded as dropped where they are not. Nothing was silently deleted: every input
of the old identity is accounted for in `lineage_of_deployment_inputs`.

_why_a_commit_and_a_release: Both, because they answer different questions and this project has been bitten
by conflating them. The COMMIT is what ID-06 checks (`git rev-parse HEAD` inside
the pinned checkout must equal it). The RELEASE is the human-readable name a
reader needs to know which upstream tag the commit belongs to. A tag can be
moved; a commit cannot, so the commit is the requirement and the release is
`upstream_patchset_sha256` from the old lock is NOT carried: its value was the
literal string 'none-no-upstream-patches', which is a statement that no patchset
exists rather than a digest of one. That belongs in `patchset` below as a
requirement (no patches), not as a hash field.

patchset.statement: This deployment applies NO patches to the pinned checkout. The checkout is read-only and its working tree must be clean; a modified checkout fails ID-06.

product_contract.name: Windows trusted-local, no sandbox
product_contract.statement: The OS user account is the execution authority boundary. No sandbox, no WSL, no Linux VM, no SSH execution world, no AppContainer, no second execution OS. Every process this deployment starts -- including the persistent IPython kernel -- runs as the invoking OS user with that user's full filesystem, network and process visibility. This deployment claims NO confinement of reads, writes, network or process visibility.
_why_the_cap_is_here: The hard continuable-child cap is a CONTRACT constant, not a build fact: V5's
product contract fixes it at 30, and `HARD_CHILD_CAPACITY = 30`
(packages/dsh-daily-work/src/capacity.ts:89) is the code's expression of it.
The requirement belongs here; the MEASURED value (and whether the mounted
subagent row's maxActiveSubagents agrees with it) belongs in the manifest,
because those are facts about one build.

launcher.requirement: the QUALIFIED launcher is the BUILT entry point (apps/cli/lib/bin.js), not the source entry point
launcher.why: G-ENV-06, reproduced 3/3: the built launcher completes a tool round trip; the source launcher dies at a '.prepare' access on an undefined value BEFORE the tool executes. A run whose only success is --help is not a run.
launcher._note: The launcher's ABSOLUTE PATH is a fact about this machine and belongs in the manifest. What belongs here is that it must be the BUILT artifact, and that its sha256 must equal the manifest's artifact_sha256.

profile.requirement: one host profile, `daily`, installed under $DSH_HOME/profiles/, composed from profiles/daily-candidate
profile.single_mode: exactly ONE selectable agent preset (ours) is exposed; the pinned checkout's shipped presets are NOT exposed
profile.why_single_mode: Round-2 brief section 1: the authorization is to stop EXPOSING the other modes from our composition. The pinned checkout is NOT edited -- its code is untouched and that is separately gated (ID-06). Removing the exposure is what this requirement means, and it is checked from the manifest's resolved graph (agent-presets row: includeShippedRoot false) and from the measured preset roster.

checkout.requirement: the pinned checkout at D:/DSH/src/dsh-src is READ-ONLY and clean
checkout.why: Editing it would trade one FAIL for a worse one and make the whole qualification meaningless. Its location is a machine-layout fact (a manifest field); its cleanliness is a requirement (ID-06).

isolation.requirement: NONE. There is no isolation domain to declare.
isolation.why: V3 makes the OS user account the authority boundary. The old lock carried `isolation_image_or_policy_digest` with the literal value 'none-trusted-local-os-user-account-is-the-execution-authority-boundary', which is a sentence, not a digest. It is recorded as a requirement statement here rather than as a hash field that could never vary.
